definition: The family of views on which the meaning of moral sentences is explained by the non-cognitive attitudes they express rather than by truth conditions. Unlike O'Connor's emotivism as he states it, contemporary (quasi-realist) expressivism may grant moral sentences truth in the minimal sense, and so need not deny that 'murder is wrong' is true.
note: No expressivist witness is pinned (e.g. Blackburn, Gibbard). Recorded so that results about O'Connor's emotivism are not read as results about expressivism in general; #182 and #185 add expressivist readings as a complete rival theory.
